profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I have worked for linux kernel developer and have maintained zram/zsmalloc of linux kernel.

Most of works are related to enhance/implement new feature of virtual memory management for linux kernel but I enjoy other parts like block/file system as well as low-level system program(ex, glibc and allocators), too.

I have worked with various solutions to optimize(ex, memory footprint and performance) in linux kernel for small memory system but I have lots of interest for huge memory system, too if it's really challenging for engineer.

I'm maintainer of zram and zsmalloc which is a virtual block device and compressed slab allocator in linux kernel and it's used heavily in embedded world for reducing memory footprint(ex, Android, TV, ChromeOS and so on).

You could see my works(ex, patch/review) related to linux kernel community via below URL

https://git.kernel.org/cgit/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/log/?qt=grep&q=minchan.kim

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Linux kernel engineer
 * page allocation/reclaim optimization/bugfix
 * vmpressure
 * optimize/bugfix CMA(Contiguous memory allocator)/memory-hotplug/compaction
 * squashfs optimization for read throughput for multiple CPU
 * per-process reclaim - http://lwn.net/Articles/545668/
 * zram/zsmalloc/zswap optimization/bugfix
 * volatile ranges/jemalloc development - http://lwn.net/Articles/522135/

memory ballooning for KVM

 * Later, became base code for ChromeOS low-memory-notifier

positions.title: Linux kernel engineer
positions.description:
Research of OS memory management in system using volatile and non-volatile RAM for main memory
 * design and implementation NVRAM module in Emulator(QEMU)
 * analysis read/write pattern of main memory in application and linux kernel
 * design and implementation page allocator and reclaim policy on NUMA(Non-Uniform Memory Access) architecture for non-volatile memory system
 * design and implementation glibc dynamic loader to support node-aware allocation for application
 * implementation and analysis performance of Hibernation/STR(Suspend-To-RAM)/STNR(Suspend-To-NVRAM) in SMDK6400/OMAP5912OSK board 

NVRAM swap system in Linux Kernel.
 * analysis of swap usage pattern with disable low memory killer of android platform
 * design and implement page allocation/swap policy when system uses NVRAM as swap in linux kernel
 * design and implement page migration of linux kernel for novoaltile memory

DTV fastboot
 * enhance glibc dynamic loader(ld.so) for reducing symbol relocation time on MIPS
 * enhance readahead of linux kernel to reduce boot-up latency
 * function reordering for putting together functions related to bootup
 * fix lots of linux kernel problems(ex, cache-aliasing, synchronization, scheduler problem, kernel memory leak and so on)

Fine-grained RSS control system for Linux
 * design and implementation test cases of RSS Quota
 * improvement accounting of page for linuxkernel

Linux kernel stack expansion for easy debugging
U-boot dvelopment for MIPS Au 1200 processor

honors.title: Embedded Linux Conference
honors.description:
ELC(Embedded Linux Conference) Speaker
San Jose, California, USA
 
Volatile ranges is a new feature for linux kernel. Normally, programs have cache on heap to perform well. It could be good thing if system memory is enough but what if system memory start to be tight? Yes, swapping, which is what everybody doesn't want. Even, many embedded devices don't have swap so they could see OOM, unfortunately. Hope volatile ranges makes userspace folks to handle cache management easy so that they overcome the problem, at last.

honors.description:
Linux Filesystem/Block/Memory Management Summit.

World best technical summit for kernel core people who have worked for filesystem/block/memory management. It's invitation-only summit.
